text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 5.5% today, closing a sharp three-day slide that wiped out nearly $40 per share. The immediate trigger appears to be escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—Iran has launched direct attacks on U.S. military installations in the Gulf region, including Kuwait, raising the risk of broader supply disruptions. While crude oil prices remain relatively stable (US oil at $89.53/barrel), the market is pricing in uncertainty: refineries are running at 95.7% capacity and storage levels are healthy, so there's no current supply crunch to support the stock, leaving it vulnerable to risk-off selling when headlines turn negative.

The sell-off also reflects a longer-term concern for refiners: oil prices aren't high enough to offset margin pressure. Diesel prices hit record highs in the UK this week (pushing inflation to a 1-year high), yet US crude hasn't spiked in response, suggesting global demand may be softening even as regional supply risks mount. For a refiner dependent on the spread between crude input costs and finished fuel prices, that's a pinch.
